title: Embodied AI mind map
scope: Perception, learning, policies, frameworks, and labs for physical intelligence. Hardware/materials only when they change the learning problem. Company nodes pull live jobs from the robotics intelligence desk.

changelog.note: Unexplored neighbors: RT-1/2, OXE, Octo, GR00T N1.5, Gemini Robotics 2, Helix, WBC, CoTracker, MASt3R, Depth Anything, sim-to-real, offline RL, PPO/SAC, cross-embodiment, LIBERO, Cosmos, MuJoCo, NVIDIA GEAR, DeepMind Robotics, Dexterity, Persona, Foundation, Eagle 2.5, RDT-1B, VQ-BeT.
Seed graph from SmolVLA, VGGT, ACT, STLight, GEN-1.5, Skild S1, and tracked US embodied-AI labs.

nodes.label: Embodied AI
nodes.brief: Models that take cameras, language, and proprioception and emit motor commands in the physical world. The bottleneck is data, latency, and generalization across objects, rooms, and robot bodies — not another transformer paper in isolation.
nodes.why: This is the center of the map. Every other node is a way to perceive, learn, act, or ship.
research_directions: Cross-embodiment foundation models (Skild, π₀, Physical Intelligence)
Async / edge inference so policies keep up with 30–100 Hz control

nodes.label: Perception
nodes.brief: Turn pixels (and maybe depth) into geometry, semantics, and tracks the policy can condition on.
nodes.why: A VLA that cannot see 3D structure or correspondences is guessing in image space.
research_directions: Self-supervised ViT features as robot backbones

nodes.label: Learning
nodes.brief: How a robot acquires a skill: copy a human, optimize a reward, or prompt a pretrained model in context.
nodes.why: ACT, DAgger, RL, and GEN-1.5 are different answers to the same compounding-error problem.

nodes.label: Policies / VLA
nodes.brief: The mapping π(cameras, language, state) → actions. Chunked BC, diffusion/flow experts, discrete tokens, or LLM-centric VLAs.
nodes.why: This is what you train in LeRobot. Size, tokenizer, and inference stack decide whether it runs on a 4090 or a cluster.

nodes.label: Systems
nodes.brief: Datasets, simulators, middleware, and inference stacks that make the papers runnable on a real arm.
nodes.why: Without LeRobotDataset, Isaac, or an async client/server, a VLA is a PDF.

nodes.label: Labs & companies
nodes.brief: Who is shipping generalist robot models or humanoids, and who is hiring. Click a lab for careers and internships from the intelligence desk.
nodes.why: Research directions and jobs are the same graph: Helix, GEN-1.5, π₀, S1 are both papers-to-read and employers.

nodes.label: Behavior cloning
nodes.brief: Supervised map from observation to expert action. Fast to train, fails when the policy leaves the demo manifold — compounding error.
nodes.why: Every LeRobot ACT/SmolVLA fine-tune is still BC at heart.

nodes.label: Compounding error
nodes.brief: A slightly wrong action, integrated at 30–50 Hz, puts the robot in states no demonstration showed. Horizon length is the enemy.
nodes.why: ACT's chunk size k is a horizon hack. DAgger is an interactive-relabel hack. GEN-1.5 tries to skip both with in-context demos.

nodes.label: Action chunking
nodes.brief: Predict k future joint commands at once, π(a_{t:t+k}|o_t). Effective horizon becomes T/k. Ablation in ACT: k=1 ~1% vs k=100 ~44% on the sim average.
nodes.why: SmolVLA, Diffusion Policy, and π₀ all still emit chunks. The fight moved to how the chunk is generated.

nodes.label: CVAE over chunks
nodes.brief: Model multimodal human demos as z ~ q(z|chunk, proprio); at test set z=0. ACT's answer to pauses and style.
nodes.why: SmolVLA drops this for flow matching. Know why before you delete z.

nodes.label: Temporal ensembling
nodes.brief: Query a new chunk every tick, average overlaps with w_i=exp(−m i). Smooth, expensive — a forward pass per control step.
nodes.why: SmolVLA async is the cheap cousin: infer only when the queue fraction drops below g.

nodes.label: Flow matching
nodes.brief: Regress a velocity field that transports noise to data along nearly straight ODE paths. Fewer function evaluations than diffusion.
nodes.why: SmolVLA's action expert is 0.75d because the path is short. Lipman et al. 2210.02747 is the paper.

nodes.label: Diffusion Policy
nodes.brief: Chi et al.: denoise an action chunk. Same chunking instinct as ACT, different generative head. LeRobot ships it next to ACT.
nodes.why: The other baseline you will actually train before a VLA.

nodes.label: ACT
nodes.brief: Zhao et al., RSS 2023. Chunk + CVAE + temporal ensemble on ALOHA. ~80M, 50 demos, fine bimanual contact. LeRobot's recommended first policy.
nodes.why: The design space later VLAs still live in.

nodes.label: SmolVLA
nodes.brief: Hugging Face, 450M. SmolVLM-2 + flow expert, community data, async inference. LIBERO-competitive with 10× smaller VLAs. SO-100 average 78.3% after community pretrain (51.7 without).
nodes.why: The open, one-GPU VLA you can actually fine-tune.

nodes.label: OpenVLA
nodes.brief: Kim et al., 7B discrete action tokens on public robot data. The heavy open baseline SmolVLA is sized against.
nodes.why: Read the tokenizer to see what flow matching is refusing.

nodes.label: π₀
nodes.brief: Physical Intelligence: Paligemma-scale VLM + diffusion/flow action expert. Cross-embodiment generalist. ~3–7× SmolVLA in params.
nodes.why: The industrial VLA recipe. GEN-1.5 and Skild S1 are the 2026 one-shot cousins.

nodes.label: GEN-1.5
nodes.brief: Generalist AI, Aug 2026. One-shot physical prompting: 3–12 s demo in a 30 s context window, no gradient step. Company-reported 59% ±10% one-shot on 10 tasks; 83% ±9% after 10 gradient steps on ~5 min of data. 100 Hz actions. Treat numbers as first-party until replicated.
nodes.why: If the claim holds, it changes the data story: skills become prompts, not datasets. Highest-priority frontier node on this map.
research_directions: How physical prompting composes with action chunking
Sim-prompt → real rollout with no sim in pretrain

nodes.label: Skild S1
nodes.brief: Skild AI foundation model: long-horizon tasks from a single video prompt, in-context, no weight update. Company-reported ~66% per-step vs 9% baseline; trained with NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Cosmos. Cross-embodiment is the pitch.
nodes.why: Same 2026 one-shot cluster as GEN-1.5, different lab. Compare claims, don't merge them.

nodes.label: VGGT
nodes.brief: CVPR 2025 Best Paper. One transformer: cameras, depth, points, tracks from 1–hundreds of views in <1 s, often beating BA-based pipelines. At test, fuse depth+cameras rather than the point-map head.
nodes.why: A perception backbone for robots that need 3D without a COLMAP ritual.

nodes.label: DINOv2
nodes.brief: Self-supervised ViT features. VGGT's patch encoder; also a common frozen vision tower in VLAs.
nodes.why: If you swap the vision encoder, you are arguing with this paper.

nodes.label: DUSt3R
nodes.brief: Two images → point maps, then global alignment for N>2. VGGT's nearest ancestor and the post-process it deletes.
nodes.why: Read the alignment section before claiming VGGT 'just does DUSt3R faster.'

nodes.label: STLight
nodes.brief: Fully convolutional future-frame prediction. Fold time into channels, STLMixer, PixelShuffle. SOTA STL at a fraction of PredRNN FLOPs (2% on KTH 10→20 for STLight-L).
nodes.why: Video dynamics / world-model cousin of robot policies. Not a VLA.

nodes.label: World models
nodes.brief: Predict future observations (or latents) to plan. STL, video DMs, and some VLA 'imagination' heads sit here. STLight is the efficient CNN end; GEN-1.5's 30 s memory is the foundation-model end.
nodes.why: A policy that can predict contact is halfway to recovering from it.

nodes.label: Reinforcement learning
nodes.brief: Learn from reward, not (only) demos. On real robots: expensive, unsafe, sample-hungry. Still the path for locomotion, recovery, and improving a cloned policy.
nodes.why: Humanoid labs mix IL for manipulation with RL for balance. Don't pretend BC replaced RL.
research_directions: RL fine-tune of a VLA action expert

nodes.label: LeRobot
nodes.brief: Hugging Face stack: LeRobotDataset, ACT, Diffusion, SmolVLA, π₀ ports, SO-100/101. Teleoperate → record → train → deploy with one CLI.
nodes.why: If you train a policy this year, you will touch this repo.

nodes.label: Isaac Lab / Sim
nodes.brief: NVIDIA robot learning sim. Skild cites it for S1 experience. GPU-parallel RL and synthetic data.
nodes.why: The sim side of foundation-model pretraining when you don't have a factory fleet.

nodes.label: ROS 2
nodes.brief: Robot middleware: topics, tf, controllers. Not a policy. Still how most arms talk to cameras and drivers.
nodes.why: LeRobot can hide it; production stacks usually don't.

nodes.label: Async inference
nodes.brief: Decouple RobotClient (pops actions at Δt) from PolicyServer (fills chunks when queue < g). SmolVLA: similar success, ~30% shorter task time (13.75s → 9.7s pick-place).
nodes.why: The systems paper hiding inside a VLA paper. Edge robots live or die here.

nodes.label: ALOHA / SO-100
nodes.brief: Low-cost bimanual (ALOHA) and 3D-printed 6-DoF (SO-100/101) teleop. Leader joints are the actions; cheap hardware is the data engine.
nodes.why: Community VLA data exists because these arms exist.

nodes.label: One-shot physical prompting
nodes.brief: Put a short sensorimotor demo in the model's context window; the robot attempts the task with no SGD. GEN-1.5's name for it; Skild S1's video prompt is the same cluster.
nodes.why: If this becomes real outside one lab, dataset size is no longer the only scaling law.

nodes.label: Figure AI
nodes.brief: San Jose humanoid + Helix VLA. Series C $39B post-money (company, 2025-09-16). Industrial + home. Heavy intern pipeline on the desk.
nodes.why: Helix is a closed VLA; careers are the open artifact.

nodes.label: Apptronik
nodes.brief: Austin. Apollo humanoid, fleet tooling, manufacturing. Largest opening count on this desk as of the last jobs scrape.

nodes.label: Agility Robotics
nodes.brief: Digit for logistics. More deployed biped-hours than most humanoid startups. Perception + locomotion stack, not a public VLA.

nodes.label: Physical Intelligence
nodes.brief: π₀ / generalist policies, no humanoid hardware of their own. The model lab behind the industrial VLA recipe.

nodes.label: Generalist AI
nodes.brief: GEN-1.5 one-shot learner. Manufacturing/manipulation across hardware. First-party evals only — keep that on the node.

nodes.label: Skild AI
nodes.brief: Omni-bodied foundation models. S1: video-prompt long-horizon tasks. Isaac Lab + Cosmos for experience.

nodes.label: Hugging Face / LeRobot
nodes.brief: Open stack + SmolVLA. Not a humanoid company; it is the public training substrate.

nodes.label: Tesla Optimus
nodes.brief: Humanoid program inside a public company. End-to-end video-to-action claims; numbers are not independently benchmarked here. Valuation on the intel desk is whole-company market cap, not Optimus.

nodes.label: Boston Dynamics
nodes.brief: Electric Atlas R&D + Spot/Stretch. Deep dynamics, not a public VLA. Acquisition-basis valuation only.

nodes.label: 1X
nodes.brief: NEO home humanoid, embodied-AI data collection. Norwegian-founded, US operations on the desk.

nodes.label: RT-2
nodes.brief: Google DeepMind 2023: fine-tune a web VLM to emit action tokens. Named the VLA. Closed, billions of params — the paper every later VLA is answering.
nodes.why: Without RT-2 there is no VLA node. SmolVLA, OpenVLA, and π₀ are size-and-openness replies.

nodes.label: RT-1
nodes.brief: 35M transformer on robot demos only, before the VLM graft. The from-scratch ancestor Octo still resembles.
nodes.why: The non-VLM baseline when someone claims we needed a 7B VLM.

nodes.label: Open X-Embodiment
nodes.brief: Pooled robot data: 21 institutions, ~22 embodiments, 1M+ trajectories, RLDS. Train set for RT-X, OpenVLA, Octo.
nodes.why: Cross-embodiment is a dataset problem first. Community LeRobot data is the cheap-arm cousin.
research_directions: How much OXE vs community SO-100 a 450M VLA actually needs

nodes.label: Octo
nodes.brief: Berkeley open transformer (~93M) on OXE, no giant VLM. Fast to fine-tune. SmolVLA sim tables still quote it.
nodes.why: The small-from-scratch generalist before SmolVLA.

nodes.label: GR00T N1.5
nodes.brief: NVIDIA GEAR, Jun 2025. Open humanoid foundation model. Eagle 2.5 VLM; NVIDIA-reported language following 46.6%→93.3% and success 43.3%→83% vs N1 on GR-1.
nodes.why: The open humanoid VLA we have not walked. Whole-body is a neighbor, not a footnote.
research_directions: Fine-tune N1.5 on SO-100 vs SmolVLA
WBC + VLA split vs Helix System 0

nodes.label: Whole-body control
nodes.brief: Lower-body RL + upper IK, or a learned high-rate controller under a VLA. NVIDIA SONIC / GR00T-WBC; Figure Helix System 0 (~1 kHz).
nodes.why: Tabletop VLAs stall on humanoids. This is the actuator-side neighbor.

nodes.label: Gemini Robotics 2
nodes.brief: DeepMind, Jul 2026. VLA for full humanoids and bi-arms; on-device variant adapts to a new body in hours; ER 2 for embodied reasoning. First-party demos. Same checkpoint on Apollo 2 and Franka.
nodes.why: Closed generalist we had not mapped. Contrast with GEN-1.5 one-shot and Helix onboard.

nodes.label: Helix / Helix 02
nodes.brief: Figure in-house VLA. Helix: 7B VLM (S2) + visuomotor transformer (S1), onboard GPU. Helix 02 (Jan 2026): System 0 learned WBC, palm cameras + tactile. First-party.
nodes.why: Vertical integration neighbor of π₀ (model-only) and SmolVLA (open).

nodes.label: CoTracker
nodes.brief: Point tracking through occlusions. VGGT feeds T_i into CoTracker2 rather than inventing a tracker.
nodes.why: Correspondence as a robot skill (grasp, tape, cable).

nodes.label: MASt3R
nodes.brief: DUSt3R evolution: two-view matching + geometry, still fused for N>2. VGGT’s pairwise competitor on pose tables.
nodes.why: Know this before quoting VGGT vs learned SfM.

nodes.label: Depth Anything
nodes.brief: Monocular depth foundation model. The single-task specialist VGGT claims to absorb. Useful when the SO-100 has one camera.
nodes.why: Cheap depth prior without multi-view.

nodes.label: Sim-to-real
nodes.brief: Train in sim (Isaac, MuJoCo), run on metal. Domain randomization, residual RL, or GEN-1.5’s claim: sim demos as prompts with no sim in pretrain.
nodes.why: Data multiplier when you do not own a factory.

nodes.label: Offline RL
nodes.brief: Learn from a logged dataset without more env steps (IQL, CQL). The path after BC when failures are in the log.
nodes.why: Humanoid logs are too expensive to throw away as not demos.

nodes.label: PPO / SAC
nodes.brief: On-policy PPO and off-policy SAC. Isaac Lab locomotion defaults. Not how you pry a condiment cup on 50 demos.
nodes.why: WBC lower body is still this. VLA did not replace it.

nodes.label: Cross-embodiment
nodes.brief: One policy, many robot bodies. OXE’s bet; Skild omni-bodied; Gemini 2 few-hour adaptation; LeRobot’s shared schema.
nodes.why: Opposite of ACT-on-one-ALOHA. Why OXE, π₀, and S1 exist.
research_directions: How much of SmolVLA community data is same-embodiment

nodes.label: LIBERO
nodes.brief: Sim suite SmolVLA quotes (Spatial/Object/Goal/Long). Binary success, 10 trials/task. Not a real robot.
nodes.why: Every VLA percentage you will cite. Know the protocol first.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Cosmos
nodes.brief: World-model / video-to-data stack Skild cites with Isaac for S1. Synthetic variety from video.
nodes.why: The data factory next to Isaac Lab, not a policy.

nodes.label: MuJoCo / MJX
nodes.brief: Contact-rich sim. ACT cube/insertion lives here. GPU MJX is the academic Isaac cousin.
nodes.why: If you ablate k on ACT, you are in MuJoCo.

nodes.label: NVIDIA GEAR
nodes.brief: GR00T, Isaac, Cosmos, SONIC WBC. The open-ish humanoid stack.

nodes.label: Google DeepMind Robotics
nodes.brief: RT-1/2, Gemini Robotics 1→2, ER 2. Named the VLA. Closed weights; public blogs.

nodes.label: Dexterity
nodes.brief: Industrial physical AI, container loading. On the intel desk. Manipulation in the wild, not a public VLA.

nodes.label: Persona AI
nodes.brief: Rugged humanoids for shipyards / heavy industry. On the ecosystem desk; learning stack not public.

nodes.label: Foundation
nodes.brief: General-purpose humanoid hardware + autonomy. On the desk; learning stack not public.

nodes.label: Eagle 2.5
nodes.brief: VLM NVIDIA starts from for GR00T N1.5 grounding. Neighbor of SigLIP/SmolVLM, not a policy.
nodes.why: If you swap SmolVLM for a robot-flavored VLM, this is the open humanoid option.

nodes.label: RDT-1B
nodes.brief: 1B diffusion transformer for bimanual manipulation. Diffusion Policy scaled; SmolVLA related-work neighbor.

nodes.label: VQ-BeT
nodes.brief: Vector-quantized behavior transformer. Another LeRobot policy class: discrete latents over chunks, not CVAE z=0.
nodes.why: The third generative head after CVAE and flow/diffusion.
